objects.definition:
typedef enum {
  /* Error status */
  CMARK_NODE_NONE,

  /* Block */
  CMARK_NODE_DOCUMENT,
  CMARK_NODE_BLOCK_QUOTE,
  CMARK_NODE_LIST,
  CMARK_NODE_ITEM,
  CMARK_NODE_CODE_BLOCK,
  CMARK_NODE_HTML_BLOCK,
  CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_BLOCK,
  CMARK_NODE_PARAGRAPH,
  CMARK_NODE_HEADING,
  CMARK_NODE_THEMATIC_BREAK,

  CMARK_NODE_FIRST_BLOCK = CMARK_NODE_DOCUMENT,
  CMARK_NODE_LAST_BLOCK = CMARK_NODE_THEMATIC_BREAK,

  /* Inline */
  CMARK_NODE_TEXT,
  CMARK_NODE_SOFTBREAK,
  CMARK_NODE_LINEBREAK,
  CMARK_NODE_CODE,
  CMARK_NODE_HTML_INLINE,
  CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_INLINE,
  CMARK_NODE_EMPH,
  CMARK_NODE_STRONG,
  CMARK_NODE_LINK,
  CMARK_NODE_IMAGE,

  CMARK_NODE_FIRST_INLINE = CMARK_NODE_TEXT,
  CMARK_NODE_LAST_INLINE = CMARK_NODE_IMAGE
} cmark_node_type;
objects.description: Enumeration of all CommonMark AST node kinds (block and inline) used by cmark.
Enumeration of list types for list nodes: none, bullet, or ordered.
Enumeration of delimiter styles for ordered lists: none, period, or parenthesis.
Opaque struct representing a node in the CommonMark AST. Actual structure is defined privately in the implementation; users manipulate via API functions.
Opaque parser object that incrementally consumes input and produces an AST rooted at a cmark_node.
Opaque iterator for walking a cmark_node tree, yielding enter/exit events.
Custom memory allocator vtable used by cmark to allocate and free all internal structures. Must remain valid for the lifetime of any objects allocated with it.
Iterator event types indicating traversal state for cmark_iter: none, done, entering a node, or exiting a node.

functions.name: cmark_markdown_to_html
functions.signature: CMARK_EXPORT char *cmark_markdown_to_html(const char *text, size_t len, int options);
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 Markdown string (text, length len) to an HTML fragment and returns a newly-allocated, null-terminated UTF-8 buffer containing the result. Caller owns and must free the returned buffer. Options is a bitmask of CMARK_OPT_* flags affecting parsing and rendering.
requirements: text is assumed to point to at least len bytes of UTF-8 data.
Caller must free the returned char* buffer.
options should be a valid bitmask composed of CMARK_OPT_* flags.

functions.name: cmark_get_default_mem_allocator
functions.description: Returns a pointer to cmark’s default memory allocator (calloc, realloc, free function table) to be used with APIs that accept a custom allocator.
requirements: Returned pointer must be treated as long-lived and not freed by the caller.

functions.name: cmark_node_is_block
functions.description: Returns true if the given node is a block node type; false otherwise.
requirements: node should be a valid cmark_node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_is_inline
functions.description: Returns true if the given node is an inline node type; false otherwise.
requirements: node should be a valid cmark_node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_is_leaf
functions.description: Returns true if the given node is a leaf node (cannot contain children); false otherwise.
requirements: node should be a valid cmark_node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new AST node of the specified type. Additional required properties (depending on type) must be set by the caller after creation. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: Caller must set any additional required properties for the chosen node type (e.g., literal content for text/code, etc.), as applicable.
Caller is responsible for freeing the node (and its subtree if populated) with cmark_node_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: cmark_node_new_with_mem
functions.description: Creates a new node using the provided memory allocator. Use the same allocator consistently for every node in a tree.
requirements: mem must point to a valid cmark_mem allocator struct.
The same allocator must be used for all nodes in a given tree.
Caller must free the node (and subtree) with cmark_node_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: cmark_node_free
functions.description: Frees the memory for the given node and all of its children.
requirements: node may be NULL-safe (unknown); if non-NULL it must be a node allocated by cmark (and with the same allocator if custom).
After calling, the node pointer must not be used.

functions.name: cmark_node_next
functions.description: Returns the next node in a sequence after node, or NULL if none. Traversal semantics are library-defined for the underlying sequence (typically next sibling in tree order).
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer belonging to a constructed tree.

functions.name: cmark_node_previous
functions.description: Returns the previous node in the sequence relative to node, or NULL if none.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer belonging to a constructed tree.

functions.name: cmark_node_parent
functions.description: Returns the parent of node, or NULL if the node has no parent (e.g., it is the root or unlinked).
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_first_child
functions.description: Returns the first child of node, or NULL if node has no children.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_last_child
functions.description: Returns the last child of node, or NULL if node has no children.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_iter_new
functions.description: Creates a new iterator that walks the tree rooted at root. The current node/event are undefined until cmark_iter_next is first called. Free the iterator with cmark_iter_free.
requirements: root must be a valid node (typically a document or subtree root).
Caller must free the iterator with cmark_iter_free.

functions.name: cmark_iter_free
functions.description: Frees a previously created iterator.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator returned by cmark_iter_new (or NULL-safe; unknown).
After calling, iter must not be used.

functions.name: cmark_iter_next
functions.description: Advances the iterator and returns the event type: CMARK_EVENT_ENTER, CMARK_EVENT_EXIT, or CMARK_EVENT_DONE. Iterators never return EXIT events for leaf nodes.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator.
Do not modify nodes except after an EXIT event, or after an ENTER event for leaf nodes (per iterator documentation).

functions.name: cmark_iter_get_node
functions.description: Returns the iterator’s current node. Valid after at least one call to cmark_iter_next and before CMARK_EVENT_DONE.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator.
Call cmark_iter_next at least once before relying on the returned node.

functions.name: cmark_iter_get_event_type
functions.description: Returns the iterator’s current event type.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator.
Call cmark_iter_next at least once to initialize event type.

functions.name: cmark_iter_get_root
functions.description: Returns the root node associated with the iterator.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator.

functions.name: cmark_iter_reset
functions.signature: CMARK_EXPORT void cmark_iter_reset(cmark_iter *iter, cmark_node *current, cmark_event_type event_type);
functions.description: Resets the iterator so that current becomes the current node and event_type the current event. The current node must be the root or a descendant of the root.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator.
current must be the iterator’s root node or a descendant of it.
event_type must be a valid cmark_event_type value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_user_data
functions.description: Returns the user data pointer previously set on the node, or NULL if none.
requirements: node must be a valid node.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_user_data
functions.description: Associates an arbitrary user data pointer with the node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be a valid node.
Check the return value; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_type
functions.description: Returns the node’s type enum value, or CMARK_NODE_NONE on error.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_type_string
functions.description: Returns a string representation of the node’s type, or "<unknown>".
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Returned string is owned by the library; do not modify or free.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_literal
functions.description: Returns the string contents of node (e.g., for text or code nodes). Returns an empty string if none is set, or NULL if node does not have string content.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_literal
functions.description: Sets the string contents of node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must support string content (e.g., appropriate node kinds).
content must point to a valid, null-terminated string.
Check the return value; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_heading_level
functions.description: Returns the heading level (1–6 typically) if node is a heading, else 0.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Only meaningful for nodes of type CMARK_NODE_HEADING.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_heading_level
functions.description: Sets the heading level for a heading node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: node must be a heading node (CMARK_NODE_HEADING).
level must be within the acceptable range for headings (exact range not specified; typically 1–6).
Check the return value; 0 indicates error.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_list_type
functions.description: Returns the list type (CMARK_BULLET_LIST, CMARK_ORDERED_LIST), or CMARK_NO_LIST if node is not a list.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Only meaningful for list nodes.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_list_type
functions.description: Sets the list type on a list node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: node must be a list node (CMARK_NODE_LIST).
type must be a valid cmark_list_type value.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_list_delim
functions.description: Returns the delimiter style for an ordered list (period or parenthesis), or CMARK_NO_DELIM if node is not a list.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Only meaningful for list nodes, especially ordered lists.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_list_delim
functions.description: Sets the delimiter style for a list node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: node must be a list node (CMARK_NODE_LIST).
delim must be a valid cmark_delim_type.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_list_start
functions.description: Returns the starting number of an ordered list node, or 0 if not ordered list.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Only meaningful for ordered list nodes.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_list_start
functions.description: Sets the starting number for an ordered list node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be an ordered list node (CMARK_NODE_LIST with CMARK_ORDERED_LIST).
start should be a non-negative integer (exact constraints not documented).
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_list_tight
functions.description: Returns 1 if the list is tight, 0 otherwise.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Only meaningful for list nodes.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_list_tight
functions.description: Sets the tightness of a list node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be a list node (CMARK_NODE_LIST).
tight should be 0 or 1 (treated as boolean).
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_fence_info
functions.description: Returns the info string from a fenced code block, or an empty string if none. Returns NULL if node is not a code block.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Only meaningful for CMARK_NODE_CODE_BLOCK.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_fence_info
functions.description: Sets the info string on a fenced code block. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be a CMARK_NODE_CODE_BLOCK.
info must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_url
functions.description: Returns the URL of a link or image node, or an empty string if none. Returns NULL if node is not a link or image.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.
Only meaningful for CMARK_NODE_LINK or CMARK_NODE_IMAGE.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_url
functions.description: Sets the URL of a link or image node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be CMARK_NODE_LINK or CMARK_NODE_IMAGE.
url must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_title
functions.description: Returns the title of a link or image node, or an empty string if none. Returns NULL if node is not a link or image.
requirements: node must be CMARK_NODE_LINK or CMARK_NODE_IMAGE for non-NULL result.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_title
functions.description: Sets the title of a link or image node. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be CMARK_NODE_LINK or CMARK_NODE_IMAGE.
title must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_on_enter
functions.description: Returns the literal text to render on entering a custom node, or an empty string if none. Returns NULL if node is not a custom node.
requirements: Node must be CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_BLOCK or CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_INLINE for non-NULL result.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_on_enter
functions.description: Sets the literal text to render when entering a custom node. Children (if any) are rendered after this text. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be a custom node (CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_BLOCK or CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_INLINE).
on_enter must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_on_exit
functions.description: Returns the literal text to render on exiting a custom node, or an empty string if none. Returns NULL if node is not a custom node.
requirements: Node must be CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_BLOCK or CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_INLINE for non-NULL result.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: cmark_node_set_on_exit
functions.description: Sets the literal text to render when exiting a custom node. Children are rendered before this text. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be a custom node (CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_BLOCK or CMARK_NODE_CUSTOM_INLINE).
on_exit must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_start_line
functions.description: Returns the source line number on which the node begins.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_start_column
functions.description: Returns the source column number at which the node begins.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_end_line
functions.description: Returns the source line number on which the node ends.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_get_end_column
functions.description: Returns the source column number at which the node ends.
requirements: node must be a valid node pointer.

functions.name: cmark_node_unlink
functions.description: Unlinks a node from its parent and siblings, removing it from the tree without freeing its memory. Use cmark_node_free to free it if desired.
requirements: node must be a valid node currently in a tree.
After unlinking, node becomes a standalone subtree and must be freed explicitly if no longer needed.

functions.name: cmark_node_insert_before
functions.description: Inserts sibling before node in the tree. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be in a tree (have a parent).
sibling must be a valid node not currently in a conflicting position (exact constraints not specified).
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_insert_after
functions.description: Inserts sibling after node in the tree. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be in a tree (have a parent).
sibling must be a valid node appropriate for insertion here.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_replace
functions.description: Replaces oldnode with newnode in the tree and unlinks oldnode (does not free it). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: oldnode must be in a tree.
newnode must be a valid node suitable for the position.
Caller must free or reuse the unlinked oldnode as appropriate.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_prepend_child
functions.description: Adds child to the beginning of node’s children list. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be a valid container node (non-leaf).
child must be a valid node.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_node_append_child
functions.description: Adds child to the end of node’s children list. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: node must be a valid container node (non-leaf).
child must be a valid node.
Check the return value.

functions.name: cmark_consolidate_text_nodes
functions.description: Consolidates adjacent text nodes under root, reducing fragmentation of text in the tree.
requirements: root must be a valid node pointer (typically a subtree root).
Call only when it is safe to modify the tree structure.

functions.name: cmark_parser_new
functions.description: Creates a new streaming parser with the given options bitmask. Free with cmark_parser_free.
requirements: options should be a valid bitmask composed of CMARK_OPT_* flags.
Caller must free the parser with cmark_parser_free.

functions.name: cmark_parser_new_with_mem
functions.description: Creates a new parser using the specified memory allocator. Equivalent to cmark_parser_new but with custom allocator control.
requirements: mem must be a valid cmark_mem pointer.
options should be a valid bitmask of CMARK_OPT_* flags.
Caller must free the parser with cmark_parser_free.

functions.name: cmark_parser_new_with_mem_into_root
functions.description: Creates a new parser that appends parsed nodes into the provided root node (children are appended after any existing children). Useful to build a single document from multiple fragments.
requirements: mem must be a valid cmark_mem pointer.
root must be a valid node to act as the AST root (typically a CMARK_NODE_DOCUMENT).
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
Caller must free the parser with cmark_parser_free.

functions.name: cmark_parser_free
functions.description: Frees a parser object created by cmark_parser_new* APIs.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser pointer (or NULL-safe; unknown).
After calling, parser must not be used.

functions.name: cmark_parser_feed
functions.signature: CMARK_EXPORT void cmark_parser_feed(cmark_parser *parser, const char *buffer, size_t len);
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of data to the streaming parser. buffer points to len bytes to be consumed.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser.
buffer must point to at least len bytes of data (assumed UTF-8 if parsing text).
May be called repeatedly before cmark_parser_finish.

functions.name: cmark_parser_finish
functions.description: Finishes parsing and returns the root of the parsed node tree. The returned tree must be freed with cmark_node_free.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser previously fed zero or more chunks.
Caller must free the returned node tree with cmark_node_free when done.

functions.name: cmark_parse_document
functions.signature: CMARK_EXPORT cmark_node *cmark_parse_document(const char *buffer, size_t len, int options);
functions.description: Parses a CommonMark document from buffer (length len) and returns the root node of the AST. Caller must free the returned tree with cmark_node_free.
requirements: buffer must point to at least len bytes of data (assumed UTF-8).
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
Caller must free the returned node tree with cmark_node_free.

functions.name: cmark_parse_file
functions.description: Parses a CommonMark document from the given FILE* and returns the root node of the AST. Caller must free the returned tree with cmark_node_free.
requirements: f must be a valid, open FILE* positioned at the beginning of the document to parse.
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
Caller must free the returned node tree with cmark_node_free.

functions.name: cmark_render_xml
functions.description: Renders the node tree as XML and returns a newly-allocated, null-terminated UTF-8 string. Caller must free the buffer.
requirements: root must be a valid node tree root.
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
Caller must free the returned char*.

functions.name: cmark_render_html
functions.description: Renders the node tree as an HTML fragment and returns a newly-allocated UTF-8 string. Caller must free the buffer.
requirements: root must be a valid node tree root.
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
Caller must free the returned char*.

functions.name: cmark_render_man
functions.signature: CMARK_EXPORT char *cmark_render_man(cmark_node *root, int options, int width);
functions.description: Renders the node tree as a groff man page (without header) and returns a newly-allocated UTF-8 string. Caller must free the buffer.
requirements: root must be a valid node tree root.
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
width specifies rendering width; exact constraints not documented.
Caller must free the returned char*.

functions.name: cmark_render_commonmark
functions.signature: CMARK_EXPORT char *cmark_render_commonmark(cmark_node *root, int options, int width);
functions.description: Renders the node tree back to CommonMark text and returns a newly-allocated UTF-8 string. Caller must free the buffer.
requirements: root must be a valid node tree root.
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
width specifies wrapping width; exact constraints not documented.
Caller must free the returned char*.

functions.name: cmark_render_latex
functions.signature: CMARK_EXPORT char *cmark_render_latex(cmark_node *root, int options, int width);
functions.description: Renders the node tree as a LaTeX document and returns a newly-allocated UTF-8 string. Caller must free the buffer.
requirements: root must be a valid node tree root.
options should be a valid CMARK_OPT_* bitmask.
width specifies rendering width; exact constraints not documented.
Caller must free the returned char*.

functions.name: cmark_version
functions.description: Returns the library version as an integer for runtime checks. Bits 16–23: major, 8–15: minor, 0–7: patch.

functions.name: cmark_version_string
functions.description: Returns the library version string for runtime checks. Also available at compile-time as CMARK_VERSION_STRING.
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not modify or free.

data_types.description: Arbitrary byte sequences intended to be interpreted as UTF-8 encoded Markdown source text. May include headings, lists, code fences, links, images, emphasis, HTML blocks/inline, etc. Input should be valid or invalid UTF-8; the parser treats bytes as UTF-8 text.
A generic null-terminated UTF-8 encoded string. No specific syntax is required beyond being a string; used for literals, titles, and custom enter/exit text.

A string representing a URL/IRI for link or image nodes. Typically follows standard URL formats (schemes like http:, https:, mailto:, data:, etc.), but may be any string; the library does not necessarily validate scheme or structure.
A file whose contents are UTF-8 encoded Markdown text. The filename itself is not significant; the parser reads the file bytes as Markdown source.

generators.generator:
import random import string from typing import List # Generator for interesting UTF-8 strings suitable for cmark string fields: # - Should be valid UTF-8 # - Null-terminated will be added by the fuzzer stub when passing c_str(), so we only provide bytes without embedded NULs # - Cover cases for literals, fence info, titles, custom enter/exit text # - Limit total size to <= 4096 bytes ASCII_PUNCT = "!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~" WHITESPACE = " \t\f\v" NEWLINES = ["\n", "\r\n", "\r"] # Some Unicode ranges and examples to exercise UTF-8 handling UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [ "π", # Greek "✓", # check mark "©®™", # symbols "𝓜𝓪𝓻𝓴𝓭𝓸𝔀𝓷", # astral plane (surrogate pairs in UTF-16) "日本語", # CJK "👩‍💻👨‍🚀", # emoji with ZWJ sequences "äöüß", # Latin-1 supplement "Привет", # Cyrillic "مرحبا", # Arabic (RTL) ] # Markdown-relevant constructs MD_LITERALS = [ "inline code: `code`", "bold and italic: **bold** and *italic*", "link: [title](https://example.com \"Title\")", "image: ![alt](img.png 'Alt Title')", "HTML block:
content
", "inline HTML: &", "autolink ", "blockquote:\n> quoted line\n> continued", "list:\n- a\n- b\n - nested", "ordered list:\n1. one\n2. two\n10) ten", "fenced code:\n```python\nprint('x')\n```", ] FENCE_INFOS = [ "", # empty info "python", "c++", "bash", "json {" + '"schema"' + "=draft7}", "mermaid", "makefile", "sh {linenos}", "lang-utf8-✓", ] TITLES = [ "Simple Title", "Title with quotes \"quoted\"", "Title with parens (example)", "Title: emoji 👩‍💻", "Multiline title\nsecond line", "RTL ‏عنوان", # includes RTL mark ] CUSTOM_TEXTS = [ "", "{custom:on_enter}", "prefix-✓-ξ", "", ] # Utility to build a random string from components ensuring size cap and no NULs def _rand_subset(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], k_range=(1, 4)) -> List[str]: k = rng.randint(k_range[0], k_range[1]) if k >= len(items): return items[:] return rng.sample(items, k) def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str: length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len) alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ASCII_PUNCT + WHITESPACE return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length)) def _maybe_newlines(rng: random.Random) -> str: s = [] for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)): s.append(rng.choice(NEWLINES)) s.append(_random_ascii(rng, 0, 8)) return ''.join(s) def _build_markdown_literal(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str: parts = [] # Mix predefined markdown, unicode, and random ascii chunks for src in _rand_subset(rng, MD_LITERALS + UNICODE_SNIPPETS, (2, 5)): parts.append(src) parts.append(_maybe_newlines(rng)) # Add some random punctuation-heavy line parts.append(_random_ascii(rng, 0, max(0, min(64, target_len // 4)))) s = '\n'.join(parts) # Trim to target_len characters (not bytes) first; we'll later encode to bytes if len(s) > target_len: s = s[:target_len] return s def _build_fence_info(rng: random.Random) -> str: # Combine a base from FENCE_INFOS with optional attributes like {key=value} base = rng.choice(FENCE_INFOS) extras = [] if rng.random() < 0.6: # add attributes-like suffixes for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)): key = rng.choice(["linenos", "hl_lines", "name", "id", "class"]) if key == "linenos": val = rng.choice(["true", "false", "1", "0"]) elif key == "hl_lines": val = '"' + ' '.join(str(rng.randint(1, 20)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))) + '"' else: val = rng.choice(["x", "main", "α", "kebab-case", "value_123"]) extras.append(f"{key}={val}") if extras: if base and not base.endswith(' '): base += ' ' base += '{' + ' '.join(extras) + '}' return base def _build_title(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str: base = rng.choice(TITLES) if rng.random() < 0.5: base += ' - ' + _random_ascii(rng, 0, 24) if len(base) > target_len: base = base[:target_len] return base def _build_custom_text(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str: parts = _rand_subset(rng, CUSTOM_TEXTS + UNICODE_SNIPPETS, (1, 4)) s = ''.join(parts) if rng.random() < 0.5: s += _maybe_newlines(rng) if len(s) > target_len: s = s[:target_len] return s def _choose_mode(rng: random.Random) -> str: # Map to target stubs: literal, fence_info, title, custom_enter/exit return rng.choice(["literal", "fence", "title", "custom"]) def _ensure_no_nul(s: str) -> str: # Remove any accidental NULs; our constructed strings should not include NUL anyway return s.replace("\x00", "") def generate(seed: int) -> bytes: rng = random.Random(seed) # Decide mode and target size limits to stay within 4096 bytes total mode = _choose_mode(rng) # Allocate a target character length conservatively below byte cap if mode == "literal": target_len = rng.randint(32, 1500) s = _build_markdown_literal(rng, target_len) elif mode == "fence": s = _build_fence_info(rng) elif mode == "title": s = _build_title(rng, rng.randint(8, 256)) else: # custom s = _build_custom_text(rng, rng.randint(8, 512)) s = _ensure_no_nul(s) # Encode to UTF-8; if somehow encoding fails (shouldn't), fallback to ASCII subset try: data = s.encode('utf-8') except UnicodeEncodeError: data = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore') # Enforce size cap (some Unicode chars are multi-byte). Trim if necessary. if len(data) > 4096: # Try trimming characters to keep valid UTF-8 boundaries # Convert back to str and slice characters s_trim = s[: max(1, int(len(s) * 4096 / max(1, len(data))))] data = s_trim.encode('utf-8') if len(data) > 4096: # As a last resort, iteratively trim bytes ensuring valid final state data = data[:4096] # Remove possible partial UTF-8 tail # Find last valid start byte position within the slice def _is_cont(b): return 0x80 <= b <= 0xBF # Trim trailing continuation bytes until a valid boundary while data and _is_cont(data[-1]): data = data[:-1] return data

import random import string import urllib.parse # Generator for valid and interesting URL strings for cmark_node_set_url # The fuzzer stub requests FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for the URL. We provide a bytes # buffer that the fuzzing harness will use as initial input. We therefore # craft a single URL per call, covering many schemes and edge cases while # remaining valid strings (UTF-8 encoded). SCHEMES = [ "http", "https", "ftp", "ftps", "mailto", "file", "data", "irc", "ssh", "tel", "news", "gopher", "ws", "wss", ] HOSTS = [ "example.com", "sub.example.com", "xn--bcher-kva.example", # punycode hint "localhost", "[::1]", "[2001:db8::1]", "192.0.2.1", ] PATH_SEGMENTS = [ "", "index.html", "a/b/c", "api/v1/resource", "~user/docs", "路径/资料", # unicode "%E2%9C%93", # percent-encoded check mark ] QUERY_KEYS = [ "q", "page", "lang", "utm_source", "utm_medium", "token", "id", "empty" ] QUERY_VALUES = [ "test", "1", "en", "fuzz", "äöü", "", "%2Fpath%2F", "a+b", "spaces here" ] FRAGMENTS = [ "", "top", "section-1", "über", "%23encoded", "!@#$%^&*()" ] USERNAMES = [ "user", "user.name", "üser", "", "admin" ] PASSWORDS = [ "pass", "p@ss", "päss", "", None ] MAILBOXES = [ "user@example.com", "John.Doe@example.com", "üßer@xn--bcher-kva.example", "first.last+tag@sub.example.com", ] DATA_MIME_TYPES = [ "text/plain", "text/html", "image/png", "application/json", "text/plain;charset=utf-8", ] DATA_PAYLOADS = [ "Hello, world!", "bold", "{\"key\":\"value\"}", "base64,SGVsbG8=", "%E2%9C%93%20ok", ] FILE_PATHS = [ "/etc/hosts", "/C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts", "/Users/test/Documents/readme.txt", "/tmp/空间.txt", ] # Utility builders def rand_choice(rng, seq): return rng.choice(seq) def rand_host(rng): # Sometimes include userinfo and port host = rand_choice(rng, HOSTS) userinfo = None if rng.random() < 0.4: user = rand_choice(rng, USERNAMES) pwd = rand_choice(rng, PASSWORDS) if pwd is None: userinfo = f"{user}@" else: userinfo = f"{user}:{pwd}@" port = "" if rng.random() < 0.5: # avoid f-string with list literal inside; choose first port_val = rng.choice(["", 0, 1, 21, 22, 80, 443, 8080, 65535]) port = f":{port_val}" return (userinfo or "") + host + port def rand_path(rng): # Mix of segments and percent-encoding base = rand_choice(rng, PATH_SEGMENTS) # Randomly add extra segments for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)): seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_~") for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))) if base and not base.endswith('/'): base += '/' base += seg if not base.startswith('/') and rng.random() < 0.6: base = '/' + base return base def rand_query(rng): if rng.random() < 0.3: return "" pairs = [] n = rng.randint(1, 4) for _ in range(n): k = rand_choice(rng, QUERY_KEYS) v = rand_choice(rng, QUERY_VALUES) k_enc = urllib.parse.quote_plus(k) v_enc = urllib.parse.quote_plus(v) pairs.append(f"{k_enc}={v_enc}") # Sometimes include key without value or repeated keys if rng.random() < 0.3: k = rand_choice(rng, QUERY_KEYS) pairs.append(urllib.parse.quote_plus(k)) return '?' + '&'.join(pairs) def rand_fragment(rng): frag = rand_choice(rng, FRAGMENTS) return '' if frag == '' else '#' + frag def build_http_like(rng, scheme): return f"{scheme}://{rand_host(rng)}{rand_path(rng)}{rand_query(rng)}{rand_fragment(rng)}" def build_mailto(rng): to = rand_choice(rng, MAILBOXES) params = [] if rng.random() < 0.7: subject = rng.choice(["Hello", "Fuzz Test", "Überraschung", "", "Symbols !@#"]) \ + (" " + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(rng.randint(0,5)))) params.append("subject=" + urllib.parse.quote(subject)) if rng.random() < 0.5: body = rand_choice(rng, ["Hi", "Line1%0ALine2", "This is a test.", "✓ ok"]) \ + (" " + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(rng.randint(0,5)))) params.append("body=" + urllib.parse.quote(body)) query = ("?" + '&'.join(params)) if params else "" return f"mailto:{to}{query}" def build_data(rng): mime = rand_choice(rng, DATA_MIME_TYPES) payload = rand_choice(rng, DATA_PAYLOADS) # Sometimes include ;base64 or parameters extra = '' if 'base64,' in payload or rng.random() < 0.3: extra = '' # already included or none elif rng.random() < 0.5: extra = ";charset=UTF-8" return f"data:{mime}{extra},{payload}" def build_file(rng): p = rand_choice(rng, FILE_PATHS) # file URLs often have three slashes for absolute paths on Unix if p.startswith('/'): return f"file://{p}" # Windows path return f"file:///{p}" def build_misc(rng, scheme): # For schemes like ssh, tel, news, gopher, ws, wss if scheme in ("tel",): num = "+" + ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(7, 15))) return f"tel:{num}" if scheme in ("ssh",): return f"ssh://{rand_host(rng)}{rand_path(rng)}" if scheme in ("news",): return f"news:{rng.choice(['comp.lang.c', 'comp.sys.unix', 'misc.test'])}" if scheme in ("gopher",): return f"gopher://{rand_host(rng)}/{rng.choice(['0','1','I','g'])}{rand_path(rng)}" if scheme in ("ws","wss"): return build_http_like(rng, scheme) if scheme in ("irc",): return f"irc://{rand_host(rng)}/{rng.choice(['#channel','nickname'])}" return build_http_like(rng, scheme) def build_url(rng): # Choose a scheme family to diversify kind = rng.choices( population=["http", "mailto", "data", "file", "misc"], weights=[40, 15, 10, 10, 25], k=1 )[0] if kind == "http": scheme = rng.choice(["http", "https", "ftp", "ftps", "ws", "wss"]) url = build_http_like(rng, scheme) elif kind == "mailto": url = build_mailto(rng) elif kind == "data": url = build_data(rng) elif kind == "file": url = build_file(rng) else: scheme = rng.choice([s for s in SCHEMES if s not in ("http","https","ftp","ftps","mailto","data","file")]) url = build_misc(rng, scheme) # Occasionally add surrounding whitespace or angle brackets which may be present in markdown link destinations if rng.random() < 0.15: url = "<" + url + ">" if rng.random() < 0.1: url = " " * rng.randint(1, 2) + url + "\t" * rng.randint(0, 1) # Ensure max length constraint to keep under 4096 bytes if len(url.encode('utf-8')) > 4000: url = url[:3000] return url def generate(seed: int) -> bytes: rng = random.Random(seed) url = build_url(rng) return url.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for UTF-8 Markdown file contents suitable for cmark_parse_file
# We try to cover many CommonMark constructs while keeping inputs valid and under 4KB.

MAX_BYTES = 4096


def _rand(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_word(r: random.Random) -> str:
    letters = string.ascii_letters
    return ''.join(r.choice(letters) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 10)))


def _rand_text(r: random.Random, min_words=3, max_words=20) -> str:
    words = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(min_words, max_words)):
        w = _rand_word(r)
        # Occasionally add punctuation
        if r.random() < 0.15:
            w += _rand(r, [',', '.', '!', '?', ':'])
        words.append(w)
    s = ' '.join(words)
    # Occasionally add emphasis markers properly paired
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        s = f"{s} {_rand(r, ['*', '_'])}{_rand_word(r)}{_rand(r, ['*', '_'])}"
    return s


def _heading(r: random.Random) -> str:
    level = r.randint(1, 6)
    return f"{'#' * level} {_rand_text(r, 1, 6)}\n"


def _setext_heading(r: random.Random) -> str:
    text = _rand_text(r, 2, 8)
    underline = '=' if r.random() < 0.5 else '-'
    return f"{text}\n{underline * r.randint(3, max(3, len(text)))}\n"


def _paragraph(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = [ _rand_text(r, 5, 30) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)) ]
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def _block_quote(r: random.Random) -> str:
    inner = _paragraph(r)
    return '\n'.join('> ' + line if line else '>' for line in inner.rstrip('\n').split('\n')) + '\n'


def _code_block_fenced(r: random.Random) -> str:
    fence = '```' if r.random() < 0.7 else '~~~'
    info = ''
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        info = ' ' + _rand(r, ['', 'python', 'c', 'cpp', 'json', 'markdown', 'sh', 'html'])
    # generate some code lines
    lines = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6)):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append('print(\"' + _rand_text(r, 1, 5).replace('"', '\\"') + '\")')
        else:
            lines.append('// ' + _rand_text(r, 2, 8))
    body = '\n'.join(lines)
    return f"{fence}{info}\n{body}\n{fence}\n"


def _indented_code_block(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = [ '    ' + _rand_text(r, 2, 8) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)) ]
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def _thematic_break(r: random.Random) -> str:
    ch = _rand(r, ['*', '-', '_'])
    count = r.randint(3, 10)
    # include optional spaces
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return (ch + ' ') * count + '\n'
    return ch * count + '\n'


def _list_block(r: random.Random, ordered: bool) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []
    start = r.randint(1, 5) if ordered and r.random() < 0.7 else 1
    delim = _rand(r, ['.', ')'])
    tight = r.random() < 0.5
    n_items = r.randint(2, 6)
    for i in range(n_items):
        if ordered:
            marker_num = start + i
            bullet = f"{marker_num}{delim} "
        else:
            bullet = _rand(r, ['- ', '* ', '+ '])
        item = bullet + _rand_text(r, 3, 12)
        lines.append(item)
        # Occasionally add a nested sub-list
        if r.random() < 0.35:
            indent = '    '
            sub_ordered = (r.random() < 0.5)
            if sub_ordered:
                sub = f"{indent}1. {_rand_text(r, 2, 8)}"
            else:
                sub = f"{indent}- {_rand_text(r, 2, 8)}"
            lines.append(sub)
        if not tight:
            lines.append('')
    # Ensure trailing newline
    return '\n'.join(lines).rstrip() + '\n'


def _link_and_image_paragraph(r: random.Random) -> str:
    text = _rand_text(r, 3, 10)
    url_schemes = ['http', 'https']
    host = _rand(r, ['example.com', 'test.org', 'localhost', 'example.net'])
    path = '/'.join(_rand_word(r).lower() for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)))
    if path:
        path = '/' + path
    url = f"{_rand(r, url_schemes)}://{host}{path}"
    title = ''
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        title = ' "' + _rand_text(r, 1, 4) + '"'
    link = f"[{_rand_text(r, 1, 4)}]({url}{title})"
    img_alt = _rand_text(r, 1, 3)
    img = f"![{img_alt}]({url}{title})"
    # Mix in code span and emphasis
    code_span = '`' + _rand(r, ['code', 'x', 'inline', _rand_word(r)]) + '`'
    emph = '*' + _rand_text(r, 1, 3) + '*'
    parts = [text, link, img, code_span, emph]
    r.shuffle(parts)
    return ' '.join(parts) + '\n'


def _html_block(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Valid simple HTML block that cmark recognizes
    tag = _rand(r, ['div', 'span', 'p', 'section'])
    cls = _rand_word(r).lower()
    inner = _rand_text(r, 2, 8)
    return f"<{tag} class=\"{cls}\">\n{inner}\n</{tag}>\n"


def _table_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # While tables are not in CommonMark core, produce a code fence with pipes to remain valid
    hdr = ' | '.join(_rand_word(r).capitalize() for _ in range(r.randint(2, 4)))
    sep = ' | '.join('---' for _ in range(hdr.count('|') + 1))
    rows = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        row = ' | '.join(_rand_text(r, 1, 3) for _ in range(hdr.count('|') + 1))
        rows.append(row)
    # Put inside fenced code to keep it valid in pure CommonMark
    content = '\n'.join([hdr, sep] + rows)
    return f"```markdown\n{content}\n```\n"


def _footnote_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Simulate definitions/refs as plain text (extensions may parse; core treats as text)
    label = _rand_word(r).lower()
    ref = f"[{label}]"
    defn = f"[{label}]: https://example.com/{label} \"{_rand_text(r,1,3)}\""
    return f"{ref} reference in text.\n\n{defn}\n"


def _heading_with_link_ref(r: random.Random) -> str:
    label = _rand_word(r)
    return f"## {_rand_text(r,1,4)} [{label}]\n\n[{label}]: https://example.com/{label.lower()}\n"


def _custom_mixture(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Assemble a document with various blocks in random order
    blocks = []
    builders = [
        _heading, _setext_heading, _paragraph, _block_quote,
        _code_block_fenced, _indented_code_block, _thematic_break,
        lambda rr: _list_block(rr, False), lambda rr: _list_block(rr, True),
        _link_and_image_paragraph, _html_block, _table_like,
        _footnote_like, _heading_with_link_ref
    ]
    r.shuffle(builders)
    for b in builders:
        if r.random() < 0.75:  # include most of them
            blocks.append(b(r))
    # Ensure document ends with newline
    doc = '\n'.join(blocks).rstrip() + '\n'
    return doc


def _ensure_size(doc: str) -> str:
    data = doc.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) <= MAX_BYTES:
        return doc
    # Truncate safely at a UTF-8 boundary by slicing bytes then decoding with ignore of partial tail
    trimmed = data[:MAX_BYTES]
    # ensure not to cut inside multi-byte sequence
    try:
        return trimmed.decode('utf-8')
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        # back off a few bytes to reach boundary
        for cut in range(MAX_BYTES - 1, MAX_BYTES - 8, -1):
            try:
                return data[:cut].decode('utf-8')
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                continue
        # as a last resort, decode with errors='ignore'
        return trimmed.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a document style
    choices = [
        _custom_mixture,
        lambda rr: _list_block(rr, False) + '\n' + _paragraph(rr) + _list_block(rr, True),
        lambda rr: _heading(rr) + _paragraph(rr) + _code_block_fenced(rr) + _link_and_image_paragraph(rr),
        lambda rr: _setext_heading(rr) + _block_quote(rr) + _indented_code_block(rr) + _thematic_break(rr),
        lambda rr: _html_block(rr) + _paragraph(rr) + _table_like(rr),
    ]
    builder = _rand(r, choices)
    doc = builder(r)
    doc = _ensure_size(doc)
    return doc.encode('utf-8')
